[...]
Norway enters the World Cup as an unproven entity. Despite having some big names in its ranks, Norway’s 28-year absence from the biggest stage leaves nothing to judge upon except recent results. For context, 16 players in the 26-man squad were not even born the last time the nation played in 1998.

# DR Congo World Cup 2026: Fixtures, key players and tactical analysis
[...]
DR Congo will compete in the World Cup for the first time since 1974 when they played as Zaire after overcoming Jamaica in the inter-confederation playoffs in March.
[...]
With a strong, experienced spine that includes a handful of established Premier League names such as Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Yoane Wissa, the Leopards could be set to spring a surprise or two on their long-awaited return to the tournament this summer.
[...]
However, with Portugal and Colombia among their Group K opponents, Sebastien Desabre’s men will have their work cut out from the off in the USA, Mexico and Canada.
[...]
Placed in CAF qualifying Group B, the Leopards finished second behind Senegal with 22 points from 10 matches. That secured a place in the second round of African qualifying and kept their World Cup hopes alive. They upset the odds twice to reach the inter-confederation play-offs, firstly beating Cameroon 1-0 in Rabat in November. Six days later, they drew 1-1 with Nigeria before winning on penalties. That victory set up a clash with Jamaica in Zapopan. The Leopards progressed thanks to Axel Tuanzebe’s extra-time winner.
[...]
Houston is the first destination for DR Congo at this summer’s World Cup. They face Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal on June 17 in an enticing opening fixture.
[...]
Next, they return to Zapopan, where they won their play-off match. There, they will take on Colombia in their second group game. The Leopards finish the group stage against Uzbekistan in Atlanta. That appears to be their most winnable fixture on paper.

highlights:
# DR Congo FIFA World Cup 2026 preview: Player to watch out for, tactics, predicted playing XI - Sportstar
[...]
# DR Congo FIFA World Cup preview: After 52-year-wait, Leopards hope for better show
[...]
DR Congo ended its pain-staking 52-year wait to feature in the World Cup when former Manchester United defender Axel Tuanzebe found himself at the right place at the right time to steer home a shot from the six-yard box to settle the Intercontinental Playoff against Jamaica.
[...]
A strong performance in the CAF qualifiers, where the side finished second behind Senegal, showed the team was more than deserving of a place in the finals. The side has grown steadily under Sebastien Desabre who had earmarked qualification to AFCON 2025 and the World Cup as his major objectives when he took over in 2022.
[...]
The Leopards have an experienced back four that can stifle any opponent on their day. Tuanzebe, Chancel Mbemba, Aaron Wan Bissaka and Arthur Masuaku have all played extensively in the Premier League and will look to scupper the attacking threat of Portugal and Colombia in Group K.
[...]
The African nation will need its forwards to fire to make a push for qualification from the group. Yoanne Wissa has two goal contributions to show in 18 appearances after a big money move to Newcastle United ahead of the recently concluded season. The lesser-heralded Fiston Mayele and Simon Banza will have to share the scoring load with Wissa and skipper Cedric Bakambu.
[...]
DR Congo’s lone World Cup appearance ended with three defeats and no goals scored in 1974. Eclipsing that dismal performance will be the first step the group will have to work towards.
[...]
Cedric Bakambu: In a career spanning 16 years, Bakambu has traversed across seven countries and has scored goals in all of them. But the number has shrunk over the last couple of years. DR Congo will need its captain to shrug off that form to make a mark in the tournament, considering his partner Yoanne Wissa has fared no better.
[...]

results.title: Norway World Cup Odds: Can the Long Shot Deliver in 2026?
highlights:
- Best Pick: Norway to reach the Round of 16
[...]
- Confidence: 3.5/5
[...]
- Best Odds: +3000 (BetOnline, outright winner)
[...]
Norway are drawn in Group I alongside France, Senegal, and Iraq. The schedule opens with a trip to Boston (Foxborough) to face Iraq on June 16, followed by a home match against Senegal in New York/New Jersey on June 22, and a final group game against France back in Boston on June 26. In Norway World Cup 2026 terms, the first two fixtures represent the clearest opportunity to bank six points before the France match. Iraq, in particular, offers Norway the chance to set an early scoring platform around Haaland.
[...]
A second-place finish in the group is the realistic floor. From there, the Round of 32 is expanded under the 2026 format, giving Norway a further knockout stage to navigate before the Round of 16, where they would likely meet a runner-up from another competitive group. A quarter-final appearance would require defeating a potential top-eight nation, which at +3000 outright represents the ceiling of what the odds are implicitly allowing for.
[...]
The outright price therefore has limited direct value given that Norway would need to beat four or five elite nations in succession. The more rational market is the stage-of-elimination: backing Norway to exit at the Round of 16 or later captures the realistic upside without requiring an implausible run. The Group I Winner market at +300 (BetOnline, Lucky Rebel) or +250 (BetNow) is also meaningful given France are the overwhelming favourites in the group and Norway will target second place.
[...]
Norway’s path through Group I sets up Iraq and Senegal as the winnable fixtures before facing France. A perfect qualifying record of 8 wins from 8 with 37 goals scored and only 5 conceded establishes the baseline: this is a team that converts quality into results when the opposition is appropriately matched. Haaland’s 23 qualifying goals alone make Norway’s attack a serious proposition against any non-elite defence. Backing Norway to progress from the group stage is the most evidence-supported Norway World Cup 2026 best pick available.
[...]
On the betting side, World Cup outright futures and group markets are already posted at BetOnline, Lucky Rebel, and BetNow. Prices shift meaningfully once the tournament begins, particularly after early group-stage results establish form. Norway’s opening match against Iraq on June 16 is a key line-mover: a comfortable Haaland-led win could shorten the Norway World Cup 2026 odds significantly across group winner and knockout progression markets, while an early stumble would lengthen them quickly. Securing prices before the tournament opens is standard practice for outright plays.
